competency_fulfillment.rationale: All three relationships are both recognised and drawn. Recognition comes through the letter H, the letter T and a ruler's two long edges; drawing comes through the ruler and set square technique for a right angle, the sliding technique for parallels, and the instruction to cross two straight lines at a slanted angle.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Parallel, intersecting and perpendicular each appear as a correct key more than once, and the relationship between two of them is probed directly by the item asking whether all perpendicular lines are also intersecting lines.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Square corner is offered alongside right angle so the technical term is glossed rather than assumed, and the set square is treated as a physical tool to slide rather than as an angle measure, which suits Grade 3 Quarter 1.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every one of the twelve samples is multiple choice, and apart from a single typed perpendicular glyph no item shows an actual drawn pair of lines to classify. Recognition is carried by verbal descriptions of letter shapes rather than by figures the pupil looks at.

competency_alignment.rationale: The harder samples move past naming into reasoning about how the categories overlap, asking whether parallel lines ever intersect and whether perpendicular implies intersecting, which develops precisely the distinctions this competency establishes.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This competency is non-numeric and the generator correctly introduces no magnitudes at all, so there is no range that could fall short of or exceed a stated ceiling.
